newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japanese men get life for drug trafficking.
newsitem.headline: Japanese men get life for drug trafficking.

text.p: Two Japanese escaped the death penalty on Friday when a Manila court sentenced them to life imprisonment for possession of more than 40 kg (88 lb) of marijuana.
Tomohisa Kimura, 37, described as unemployed and originally from Fukuoka, and 51-year-old businessman Akira Kizaki, from Tokyo, were arrested in 1994.
They were caught after trying to sell marijuana to a policeman posing as a dealer in a central Manila supermarket carpark.
Judge Eriberto Rosario said the life sentence was due to "the absence of mitigating or aggravating circumstances".
Possession of more than 750 grammes can carry the death penalty.
He also fined them 500,000 pesos ($19,000) each and ordered they be deported at the end of their sentence. Life imprisonment is usually 20-30 years.
Both men, who insisted they were innocent, looked shocked after the verdict was read and Kimura said they would appeal.
"I don't know what to do. I find the verdict wrong," Kimura told reporters.
He had to translate the verdict, which was read in English, to his companion.
Kimura has a separate case pending on charges of illegal possession of ammunition.
